blocks.prompt: 1 (i) Plot the following point: \((2,\ 75^{\circ})\).
blocks.explanation: Yeh sawal polar coordinates ka hai: humein ek point graph par lagana (plot karna) hai. Dekhiye, polar point \((r, \theta)\) do baatein batata hai: kis taraf jaana hai (angle \(\theta\)) aur kitni door jaana hai (\(|r|\)). Bilkul aise jaise koi aap ko rasta bataye: "is taraf mudo aur itne qadam chalo". Is part mein r positive hai, is liye angle wali ray par seedha aage chalna hai. Plan yeh hai: angle samjhein, r ka sign dekhein, phir x aur y nikaal kar point bilkul theek jagah lagayein aur aakhir mein faasla check karein.
steps:
Given (diya gaya hai): polar point \((2,\ 75^{\circ})\), yani \(r = 2\) aur \(\theta = 75^{\circ}\).
To find (maloom karna hai): yeh point polar plane par kahan aata hai, aur use plot karna.
Method (tareeqa): pehle polar axis (yani positive x-axis) se angle \(\theta\) jitna ghoomein: \(\theta\) positive ho to anticlockwise (ghari ki suiyon ke ulat), negative ho to clockwise (ghari ki suiyon ki taraf). Phir us ray (seedhi lakeer jo O se shuru ho kar ek taraf jaati hai) par \(|r|\) units chalein. Agar \(r\) negative ho to isi ray ki bajaye ulti (opposite) ray par chalein.

r ka sign dekhein
\(r = 2 > 0\), is liye point isi \(75^{\circ}\) wali ray par hoga.
Kyun: positive r ka matlab hai ray ke saath aage ki taraf chalna. Angle pehle hi degrees mein hai, aur \(75^{\circ}\) first quadrant mein hai (\(0^{\circ}\) aur \(90^{\circ}\) ke darmiyan), is liye point upar-daayein taraf aayega, y-axis ke kaafi qareeb.

Rectangular coordinates nikaalein (taake point bilkul sahi jagah lage)
\[x = 2\cos 75^{\circ}\]
\[x \approx 2(0.2588) \approx 0.52\]
\[y = 2\sin 75^{\circ}\]
\[y \approx 2(0.9659) \approx 1.93\]
Kyun: \(x = r\cos\theta\) aur \(y = r\sin\theta\) wohi point x aur y ki zubaan mein de dete hain. Graph paper par x aur y se point lagana zyada pakka hota hai, aur is se quadrant bhi confirm ho jata hai: pehla (first) quadrant. Dono x aur y positive hain, jo first quadrant ki pehchaan hai. \(\cos 75^{\circ}\) aur \(\sin 75^{\circ}\) standard angles nahi, is liye calculator ki values li hain.

Point plot karein
O se \(75^{\circ}\) par ray kheenchein (protractor polar axis par rakh kar angle naapein), phir is ray par O se 2 units door point lagayein. Yeh point taqreeban \((0.52,\ 1.93)\) par aayega.
Kyun: polar coordinates mein angle direction batata hai aur \(|r|\) O se faasla. Polar grid ke circles (rings) faasla naapne mein madad dete hain: point ko us ring par lagayein jis ka radius \(|r|\) hai.

Tasdeeq (check):
Ab khud se poochiye: kya hamara point O se theek \(|r|\) faasle par hai? Pythagoras se faasle ka square \(x^{2} + y^{2}\) hota hai:
\[0.52^{2} + 1.93^{2} \approx 3.99 \approx 4\]
aur yeh \(2^{2} = 4\) ke barabar hai, yani point sahi jagah hai. (Chhota sa farq sirf decimal rounding ki wajah se hai.)
blocks.final_answer: Point \(75^{\circ}\) wali ray par, O se 2 units door, pehle (first) quadrant mein, taqreeban \((0.52,\ 1.93)\) par hai. Matlab: polar axis se \(75^{\circ}\) anticlockwise ghoom kar 2 qadam aage.

blocks.prompt: 1 (ii) Plot the following point: \((-3,\ 120^{\circ})\).
blocks.explanation: Yeh sawal polar coordinates ka hai: humein ek point plot karna hai. Polar point \((r, \theta)\) mein \(\theta\) direction batata hai aur \(|r|\) origin O se faasla. Is part ki khaas baat yeh hai ke r negative hai. Negative r ka matlab hai: angle ki taraf munh kar ke ulte qadam chalna, yani O se guzar kar bilkul ulti taraf pohanchna. Bohat se students yahan point ko angle wali ray par hi laga dete hain, jo ghalat hai. Plan: angle ko degrees mein samjhein, negative r ki wajah se direction mein \(180^{\circ}\) jama karein, x aur y nikaalein, point lagayein aur faasla check karein.
steps:
Given (diya gaya hai): polar point \((-3,\ 120^{\circ})\), yani \(r = -3\) aur \(\theta = 120^{\circ}\).
To find (maloom karna hai): yeh point polar plane par kahan aata hai, aur use plot karna.
Method (tareeqa): pehle polar axis (yani positive x-axis) se angle \(\theta\) jitna ghoomein: \(\theta\) positive ho to anticlockwise (ghari ki suiyon ke ulat), negative ho to clockwise (ghari ki suiyon ki taraf). Phir us ray (seedhi lakeer jo O se shuru ho kar ek taraf jaati hai) par \(|r|\) units chalein. Agar \(r\) negative ho to isi ray ki bajaye ulti (opposite) ray par chalein.

Negative r ko handle karein
Yahan \(r\) negative hai. Is ka matlab hai ke angle wali ray ki taraf munh kar ke hum ulte qadam chalenge, yani O se guzar kar bilkul ulti taraf. Ulti taraf ka matlab direction mein \(180^{\circ}\) jama karna:
\[120^{\circ} + 180^{\circ} = 300^{\circ}\]
\[(-3,\ 120^{\circ}) = (3,\ 300^{\circ})\]
Kyun: \((-r, \theta)\) aur \((r, \theta + 180^{\circ})\) ek hi point ke do naam hain. Socho aap kisi darwaze ki taraf munh kar ke khare hain aur 3 qadam peeche hat-te hain: aap darwaze se ulti taraf pohanch jaate hain. Is tarah given angle \(120^{\circ}\) ki bajaye asal direction \(300^{\circ}\) ban jaati hai, aur ab faasla positive \(|r|\) hai. \(120^{\circ}\) second quadrant mein hai, is liye ulti taraf fourth quadrant mein pohanchte hain.
Dhyan dein: \(180^{\circ}\) jama karna hai, sirf angle ka sign badalna nahi. Angle ka sign badalne se point x-axis ke mirror mein chala jata hai, jo bilkul alag point hai.

Rectangular coordinates nikaalein (taake point bilkul sahi jagah lage)
\[x = -3\cos 120^{\circ}\]
\[x = -3\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = \dfrac{3}{2}\]
\[y = -3\sin 120^{\circ}\]
\[y = -3\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) \approx -2.60\]
Kyun: \(x = r\cos\theta\) aur \(y = r\sin\theta\) wohi point x aur y ki zubaan mein de dete hain. Graph paper par x aur y se point lagana zyada pakka hota hai, aur is se quadrant bhi confirm ho jata hai: chautha (fourth) quadrant. Yahan \(\cos 120^{\circ} = -\frac{1}{2}\) aur \(\sin 120^{\circ} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\) hain (standard angle, reference angle \(60^{\circ}\)); negative r se zarb dene par x positive aur y negative ho gaya.
Dhyan dein: yahan r ko us ke sign samet (jaisa diya hai) aur asal given angle ke saath istemal kiya hai; dono tareeqon (negative r ke saath given angle, ya positive \(|r|\) ke saath nayi direction) se bilkul wohi x aur y aate hain.

Point plot karein
O se \(300^{\circ}\) par ray kheenchein (protractor polar axis par rakh kar angle naapein), phir is ray par O se 3 units door point lagayein. Yeh point taqreeban \((1.5,\ -2.60)\) par aayega.
Kyun: polar coordinates mein angle direction batata hai aur \(|r|\) O se faasla. Polar grid ke circles (rings) faasla naapne mein madad dete hain: point ko us ring par lagayein jis ka radius \(|r|\) hai.

Tasdeeq (check):
Ab khud se poochiye: kya hamara point O se theek \(|r|\) faasle par hai? Pythagoras se faasle ka square \(x^{2} + y^{2}\) hota hai:
\[1.5^{2} + 2.60^{2} \approx 9.01 \approx 9\]
aur yeh \(3^{2} = 9\) ke barabar hai, yani point sahi jagah hai. (Chhota sa farq sirf decimal rounding ki wajah se hai.)
blocks.final_answer: Point \(300^{\circ}\) wali ray par, O se 3 units door, chauthay (fourth) quadrant mein, taqreeban \((1.5,\ -2.60)\) par hai; yeh wohi point hai jo \((3,\ 300^{\circ})\). Yani \(120^{\circ}\) ki taraf munh kar ke 3 qadam peeche.

blocks.prompt: 2 (i) Express the complex number in polar form: \(4 + 3i\).
blocks.explanation: Yeh polar form ka sawal hai: humein \(z = x + iy\) ko \(r(\cos\theta + i\sin\theta)\) ki shakal mein likhna hai. Polar form asal mein point ka pata 'kitni door aur kis taraf' ki zubaan mein batata hai: r origin se faasla (modulus) hai aur \(\theta\) direction (argument). Plan: (1) x aur y ke sign se quadrant pehchanein, (2) \(r = \sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2}}\) se modulus nikaalein, (3) \(\tan^{-1}|y/x|\) se reference angle (x-axis ke saath chhota angle) lein, (4) quadrant ke mutabiq use principal argument (\(-\pi < \theta \le \pi\)) mein badlein. Yahan dono parts positive hain, is liye kaam seedha hai, lekin y/x aur x/y ka farq yaad rakhna hai: answer key ne yahin ghalti ki hai.
steps:
Given (diya gaya hai): \(z = 4 + 3i\), yani \(x = 4\) (real part), \(y = 3\) (imaginary part).
To find (maloom karna hai): modulus r aur principal argument \(\theta\), taake \(z = r(\cos\theta + i\sin\theta)\) likh sakein.
Method (tareeqa): \(r = \sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}\) (Pythagoras), aur \(\theta\) ke liye pehle reference angle, phir quadrant ka rule.

Quadrant pehchanein
\(x = 4 > 0\) aur \(y = 3 > 0\): point \((4, 3)\) pehle (first) quadrant mein hai.
Kyun: First quadrant mein calculator ka \(\tan^{-1}(y/x)\) hi asal argument hota hai; koi adjustment nahi chahiye. Doosre quadrants mein calculator dhoka de sakta hai, is liye hum hamesha pehle quadrant dekhte hain.

Modulus nikaalein
\[r = \sqrt{4^{2} + 3^{2}}\]
\[r = \sqrt{16 + 9} = \sqrt{25} = 5\]
Kyun: r point \((4, 3)\) ka O se faasla hai. x aur y ek right-angled triangle ki do sides hain aur r us ka hypotenuse (kaan), is liye Pythagoras lagta hai. Yeh mashhoor 3-4-5 triangle hai.

Argument nikaalein
\[\theta = \tan^{-1}\dfrac{3}{4}\]
\[\theta \approx 36.87^{\circ}\]
(radian mein \(\theta \approx 0.6435\))
Kyun: argument ke liye \(\tan\theta = \dfrac{y}{x} = \dfrac{3}{4}\) hota hai, yani 'upar ki doori' taqseem 'daayein ki doori'. \(\frac{3}{4}\) koi standard value nahi, is liye calculator se decimal angle liya.
Dhyan dein: y upar (numerator) aur x neeche (denominator) aata hai. Agar ulta \(\tan^{-1}\frac{4}{3}\) le liya to \(53.13^{\circ}\) aata hai, jo \(3 + 4i\) ka angle hai, \(4 + 3i\) ka nahi.

Polar form likhein
\[z = 5(\cos 36.87^{\circ} + i\sin 36.87^{\circ})\]
Kyun: bas r aur \(\theta\) ko \(r(\cos\theta + i\sin\theta)\) mein rakh diya.

Tasdeeq (check):
Polar form se wapas x aur y nikaal kar dekhte hain ke wohi number milta hai ya nahi:
\[5\cos 36.87^{\circ} \approx 5(0.8) = 4\]
\[5\sin 36.87^{\circ} \approx 5(0.6) = 3\]
Hamein wapas \(4 + 3i\) mil gaya, is liye jawab sahi hai.
blocks.final_answer: \(4 + 3i = 5(\cos 36.87^{\circ} + i\sin 36.87^{\circ})\), yani \(r = 5\), \(\theta = \tan^{-1}\frac{3}{4} \approx 36.87^{\circ}\) (0.6435 rad). Matlab: point O se 5 units door, polar axis se \(36.87^{\circ}\) upar hai.

blocks.prompt: 2 (iv) Express the complex number in polar form: \(-\frac{5}{2} - \frac{5\sqrt{3}}{2}i\).
blocks.explanation: Yeh polar form ka sawal hai: humein \(z = x + iy\) ko \(r(\cos\theta + i\sin\theta)\) ki shakal mein likhna hai. Polar form asal mein point ka pata 'kitni door aur kis taraf' ki zubaan mein batata hai: r origin se faasla (modulus) hai aur \(\theta\) direction (argument). Plan: (1) x aur y ke sign se quadrant pehchanein, (2) \(r = \sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2}}\) se modulus nikaalein, (3) \(\tan^{-1}|y/x|\) se reference angle (x-axis ke saath chhota angle) lein, (4) quadrant ke mutabiq use principal argument (\(-\pi < \theta \le \pi\)) mein badlein. steps:
Given (diya gaya hai): \(x = -\frac{5}{2}\), \(y = -\frac{5\sqrt{3}}{2}\).
To find (maloom karna hai): modulus r aur principal argument \(\theta\), taake \(z = r(\cos\theta + i\sin\theta)\) likh sakein.
Method (tareeqa): \(r = \sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}\) (Pythagoras), aur \(\theta\) ke liye pehle reference angle, phir quadrant ka rule.

Quadrant pehchanein
\(x < 0\) aur \(y < 0\): teesra (third) quadrant.
Kyun: \(\frac{y}{x}\) mein dono minus cancel ho jaate hain, is liye calculator ko lagta hai ke point first quadrant mein hai. Woh do minus nahi dekh sakta; hamein khud angle ko third quadrant mein le jaana hai.

Modulus nikaalein
\[r = \sqrt{\dfrac{25}{4} + \dfrac{75}{4}}\]
\[r = \sqrt{\dfrac{100}{4}} = \sqrt{25} = 5\]
Kyun: square karne se minus sign khatam ho jata hai, kyunke faasla kabhi negative nahi hota. \(\left(\frac{5\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)^{2} = \frac{25 \times 3}{4} = \frac{75}{4}\).

Reference angle nikaalein
\[\alpha = \tan^{-1}\dfrac{5\sqrt{3}/2}{5/2} = \tan^{-1}\sqrt{3}\]
\[\alpha = \dfrac{\pi}{3}\]
Kyun: reference angle \(\alpha\) sirf x aur y ke size (bina sign) se nikalta hai; yeh x-axis ke saath bana chhota angle hai. \(\tan^{-1}\sqrt{3} = 60^{\circ} = \frac{\pi}{3}\).

Principal argument nikaalein
\[\theta = -(\pi - \alpha)\]
\[\theta = -\left(\pi - \dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = -\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\]
Kyun: principal argument \(-\pi\) aur \(\pi\) ke darmiyan hona chahiye. Third quadrant tak pohanchne ke do raaste hain: anticlockwise \(\pi + \frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{4\pi}{3}\), ya clockwise \(-\frac{2\pi}{3}\). Dono ek hi direction hain, lekin \(\frac{4\pi}{3}\) range se bahar hai, is liye principal value \(-\frac{2\pi}{3}\) hai.
Dhyan dein: third quadrant mein principal argument hamesha negative hota hai: \(\theta = -(\pi - \alpha)\).

Polar form likhein
\[z = 5\left(\cos\left(-\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right) + i\sin\left(-\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right)\right)\]
Kyun: \(r(\cos\theta + i\sin\theta)\) mein principal argument rakha.

Tasdeeq (check):
\[5\cos\left(-\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right) = 5\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = -\dfrac{5}{2}\]
\[5\sin\left(-\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right) = -\dfrac{5\sqrt{3}}{2}\]
Dono parts z se mil gaye, is liye jawab sahi hai.
blocks.final_answer: \(z = 5\left(\cos\left(-\frac{2\pi}{3}\right) + i\sin\left(-\frac{2\pi}{3}\right)\right)\); yeh wohi number hai jo \(5\left(\cos\frac{4\pi}{3} + i\sin\frac{4\pi}{3}\right)\), jo answer key ki form hai. Dono sahi hain; principal value \(-\frac{2\pi}{3}\) hai.

blocks.prompt: 3 (i) Convert the complex number z into the rectangular form \(x + iy\): \(4\left(\cos\frac{5\pi}{3} + i\sin\frac{5\pi}{3}\right)\).
blocks.explanation: Yeh Sawal 2 ka ulta kaam hai: yahan humein r (faasla) aur \(\theta\) (direction) diye gaye hain, aur point ka 'address' x aur y mein likhna hai, yani \(x + iy\). Formula seedha hai: \(x = r\cos\theta\) aur \(y = r\sin\theta\). Asal mehnat angle par hai: plan yeh hai ke (1) angle ko degrees mein badal kar aasaan banayein (poore chakkar hata kar), (2) quadrant dekh kar cos aur sin ke sign tay karein, (3) reference angle se un ki values lein, (4) r se zarb dein, aur aakhir mein modulus check karein. Is part mein answer key ne sin ka sign ghalat liya hai, is liye quadrant wala qadam bohat dhyan se dekhiye.
steps:
Given (diya gaya hai): \(r = 4\), \(\theta = \frac{5\pi}{3}\).
To find (maloom karna hai): z ko \(x + iy\) (rectangular form) mein likhna.
Method (tareeqa): \(x = r\cos\theta\), \(y = r\sin\theta\). Yeh is liye lagta hai ke cos 'daayein-baayein' ka hissa aur sin 'upar-neeche' ka hissa deta hai.

Angle badlein aur quadrant pehchanein
\[\dfrac{5\pi}{3} = 5 \times 60^{\circ} = 300^{\circ}\]
\(300^{\circ}\) chauthay (fourth) quadrant mein hai (\(270^{\circ}\) aur \(360^{\circ}\) ke darmiyan); reference angle \(360^{\circ} - 300^{\circ} = 60^{\circ}\).
Kyun: \(\frac{\pi}{3} = 60^{\circ}\), to \(\frac{5\pi}{3} = 300^{\circ}\). Fourth quadrant mein cos positive aur sin negative hota hai. Yaad rakhiye: first quadrant mein sab positive, second mein sirf sin positive, third mein sirf tan positive (cos aur sin dono negative), fourth mein sirf cos positive.

cos aur sin ki values
\[\cos 300^{\circ} = \cos 60^{\circ} = \dfrac{1}{2}\]
\[\sin 300^{\circ} = -\sin 60^{\circ} = -\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\]
Kyun: size (value) reference angle \(60^{\circ}\) se aata hai, aur sign quadrant se.
Dhyan dein: \(\sin 300^{\circ}\) negative hai. Agar yeh minus bhool gaye to jawab \(2 + 2\sqrt{3}i\) ban jayega, jo answer key ki ghalti hai.

r se zarb dein
\[z = 4\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) + 4\left(-\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)i\]
\[z = 2 - 2\sqrt{3}\,i\]
Kyun: \(x = r\cos\theta = 4 \times \frac{1}{2} = 2\) aur \(y = r\sin\theta = 4 \times \left(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = -2\sqrt{3}\).

Tasdeeq (check):
Jawab ka modulus wapas r hona chahiye:
\[|z|^{2} = 2^{2} + (2\sqrt{3})^{2} = 4 + 12 = 16\]
is liye \(|z| = 4 = r\). Aur point \((2, -2\sqrt{3})\) fourth quadrant mein hai, jaisa angle keh raha tha. Sahi.
blocks.final_answer: \(z = 2 - 2\sqrt{3}\,i \approx 2 - 3.46i\): yeh point fourth quadrant mein, O se 4 units door hai.

Angle badlein aur quadrant pehchanein
\[\dfrac{7\pi}{6} = 7 \times 30^{\circ} = 210^{\circ}\]
Teesra (third) quadrant, reference angle \(210^{\circ} - 180^{\circ} = 30^{\circ}\).
Kyun: \(\frac{\pi}{6} = 30^{\circ}\), to \(\frac{7\pi}{6} = 210^{\circ}\), jo \(180^{\circ}\) se thora aage hai. Third quadrant mein cos aur sin dono negative hain.

\[z = \dfrac{3}{2}\left(-\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) + \dfrac{3}{2}\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)i\]

blocks.prompt: 4 (i) If \(z_1 = 9\left(\cos\frac{5\pi}{4} + i\sin\frac{5\pi}{4}\right)\) and \(z_2 = 5\left(\cos\frac{\pi}{3} + i\sin\frac{\pi}{3}\right)\), find \(z_1 + z_2\).
blocks.explanation: Yeh do polar numbers ka jama (sum) hai. Polar form zarb aur taqseem ke liye behtareen hai, lekin jama ke liye nahi. Is liye plan yeh hai: pehle \(z_1\) aur \(z_2\) dono ko \(x + iy\) mein badlein, phir real parts aapas mein aur imaginary parts aapas mein jama karein. Aakhir mein ek rough drawing se check karenge ke jawab sahi taraf hai.
steps:
Given (diya gaya hai): \(z_1 = 9\,\text{cis}\,\frac{5\pi}{4}\), \(z_2 = 5\,\text{cis}\,\frac{\pi}{3}\). (cis ek chhota naam hai: \(\text{cis}\,\theta = \cos\theta + i\sin\theta\).)
To find (maloom karna hai): \(z_1 + z_2\).
Method (tareeqa): dono ko rectangular form (\(x + iy\)) mein badlein, phir part by part kaam karein.

\(z_1\) aur \(z_2\) ko rectangular form mein likhein
\(\frac{5\pi}{4} = 225^{\circ}\) (third quadrant, jahan cos aur sin dono \(-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\) hain, reference angle \(45^{\circ}\)); \(\frac{\pi}{3} = 60^{\circ}\) (first quadrant).
\[z_1 = 9\left(-\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2} - \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}i\right)\]
\[z_1 = -\dfrac{9\sqrt{2}}{2} - \dfrac{9\sqrt{2}}{2}i\]
\[z_1 \approx -6.364 - 6.364i\]
\[z_2 = 5\left(\dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}i\right)\]
\[z_2 = \dfrac{5}{2} + \dfrac{5\sqrt{3}}{2}i \approx 2.5 + 4.330i\]
Kyun: polar form mein jama (addition) aur tafreeq (subtraction) ka koi seedha rule nahi hai. Socho do log alag alag directions mein chal rahe hon: un ke faasle seedhe jama nahi hote. Is liye pehle dono numbers ko \(x + iy\) mein badalte hain, jahan real ko real se aur imaginary ko imaginary se jora ja sakta hai.
Dhyan dein: \(225^{\circ}\) third quadrant mein hai, is liye cos aur sin dono ke saath minus lagega.

Real parts aur imaginary parts jama karein
\[x = \dfrac{5}{2} - \dfrac{9\sqrt{2}}{2} = \dfrac{5 - 9\sqrt{2}}{2}\]
\[y = \dfrac{5\sqrt{3}}{2} - \dfrac{9\sqrt{2}}{2} = \dfrac{5\sqrt{3} - 9\sqrt{2}}{2}\]
Kyun: \((a + ib) + (c + id) = (a + c) + i(b + d)\). Bilkul aise jaise rupay rupay se aur paise paise se jama karte hain: real aur imaginary kabhi aapas mein nahi milte.

Decimals mein badlein
\[x \approx -6.364 + 2.5 = -3.864\]
\[y \approx -6.364 + 4.330 = -2.034\]
Kyun: yeh angles mil kar koi standard angle nahi banate, is liye decimal jawab sab se wazeh hai. Rounding sirf aakhir mein ki hai taake ghalti jama na ho.

Tasdeeq (check):
Rough drawing banayein: \(z_1\) neeche-baayein taraf lamba (9 units) hai, \(z_2\) upar-daayein taraf chhota (5 units). Jama ka nateeja lambe wale ki taraf, yani neeche-baayein hona chahiye. \(-3.86 - 2.03i\) neeche-baayein hai. Sahi.
Kyun: jama ka modulus \(9 + 5 = 14\) se zyada nahi ho sakta; hamara jawab chhota hai, theek. Answer key ka \(-6.54 + 15.32i\) upar ki taraf aur 16 se lamba hai, is liye woh ghalat hai.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Answer key \(-6.54 + 15.32i\) deti hai, jo in do numbers ka jama nahin (is ka modulus 16 se zyada hai, jab ke \(|z_1 + z_2| \le 9 + 5 = 14\)). Sahi jawab \(-3.86 - 2.03i\) hai.

blocks.prompt: 4 (ii) If \(z_1 = 9\left(\cos\frac{5\pi}{4} + i\sin\frac{5\pi}{4}\right)\) and \(z_2 = 5\left(\cos\frac{\pi}{3} + i\sin\frac{\pi}{3}\right)\), find \(z_1 - z_2\).

Sab se zyada ghaltiyan signs mein hoti hain: minus \(z_2\) ke dono parts par lagta hai. Aakhir mein ek khoobsurat check karenge: \((z_1 + z_2) + (z_1 - z_2) = 2z_1\).
steps:
Given (diya gaya hai): \(z_1 = 9\,\text{cis}\,\frac{5\pi}{4}\), \(z_2 = 5\,\text{cis}\,\frac{\pi}{3}\). (cis ek chhota naam hai: \(\text{cis}\,\theta = \cos\theta + i\sin\theta\).)
To find (maloom karna hai): \(z_1 - z_2\).
Method (tareeqa): dono ko rectangular form (\(x + iy\)) mein badlein, phir part by part kaam karein.

\(z_1\) aur \(z_2\) ko rectangular form mein likhein
\(\frac{5\pi}{4} = 225^{\circ}\) (third quadrant, jahan cos aur sin dono \(-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\) hain, reference angle \(45^{\circ}\)); \(\frac{\pi}{3} = 60^{\circ}\) (first quadrant).
\[z_1 = 9\left(-\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2} - \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}i\right)\]
\[z_1 = -\dfrac{9\sqrt{2}}{2} - \dfrac{9\sqrt{2}}{2}i\]
\[z_1 \approx -6.364 - 6.364i\]
\[z_2 = 5\left(\dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}i\right)\]
\[z_2 = \dfrac{5}{2} + \dfrac{5\sqrt{3}}{2}i \approx 2.5 + 4.330i\]
Kyun: polar form mein jama (addition) aur tafreeq (subtraction) ka koi seedha rule nahi hai. Socho do log alag alag directions mein chal rahe hon: un ke faasle seedhe jama nahi hote. Is liye pehle dono numbers ko \(x + iy\) mein badalte hain, jahan real ko real se aur imaginary ko imaginary se jora ja sakta hai.

Real parts aur imaginary parts minus karein
\[x = -\dfrac{9\sqrt{2}}{2} - \dfrac{5}{2} = -\dfrac{9\sqrt{2} + 5}{2}\]
\[y = -\dfrac{9\sqrt{2}}{2} - \dfrac{5\sqrt{3}}{2} = -\dfrac{9\sqrt{2} + 5\sqrt{3}}{2}\]
Kyun: \((a + ib) - (c + id) = (a - c) + i(b - d)\).
Dhyan dein: minus sign \(z_2\) ke real aur imaginary dono hisson par lagta hai. Sirf real part se minus kar ke imaginary part jama kar dena bohat aam ghalti hai.

Decimals mein badlein
\[x \approx -6.364 - 2.5 = -8.864\]
\[y \approx -6.364 - 4.330 = -10.694\]
Kyun: rounding aakhir mein karne se jawab zyada durust rehta hai.

Tasdeeq (check):
Pichle part ka jawab is ke saath jama karein; \((z_1 + z_2) + (z_1 - z_2) = 2z_1\) hona chahiye:
\[(-3.864 - 8.864) + (-2.034 - 10.694)i\]
\[= -12.728 - 12.728i = 2z_1\]
aur \(2z_1 \approx -12.728 - 12.728i\) hi hai. Sahi.
Kyun: \(z_2\) aur \(-z_2\) cancel ho jaate hain. Yeh check dono parts (i) aur (ii) ko ek saath pakka kar deta hai.

blocks.prompt: 4 (iii) If \(z_1 = 9\left(\cos\frac{5\pi}{4} + i\sin\frac{5\pi}{4}\right)\) and \(z_2 = 5\left(\cos\frac{\pi}{3} + i\sin\frac{\pi}{3}\right)\), find \(z_1 \cdot z_2\).
blocks.explanation: Ab zarb (product) hai, aur yahan polar form apna kamaal dikhati hai. Product rule: moduli (lengths) zarb karo aur arguments (angles) jama karo. Plan: \(r_1 r_2\) nikaalein, \(\theta_1 + \theta_2\) nikaalein, angle ko principal range \((-\pi, \pi]\) mein laayein, phir \(x + iy\) bhi likhein aur rectangular zarb se check karein.
steps:
Given (diya gaya hai): \(r_1 = 9\), \(\theta_1 = \frac{5\pi}{4}\); \(r_2 = 5\), \(\theta_2 = \frac{\pi}{3}\).
To find (maloom karna hai): \(z_1 z_2\).
Method (tareeqa): \(z_1 z_2 = r_1 r_2[\cos(\theta_1 + \theta_2) + i\sin(\theta_1 + \theta_2)]\), kyunke dono numbers pehle hi polar form mein hain.

Moduli zarb karein
\[r_1 r_2 = 9 \times 5 = 45\]
Kyun: product ka modulus dono moduli ka zarb hota hai: \(|z_1 z_2| = |z_1||z_2|\). Lambaiyan zarb hoti hain.

Arguments jama karein
\[\dfrac{5\pi}{4} + \dfrac{\pi}{3} = \dfrac{15\pi}{12} + \dfrac{4\pi}{12}\]
\[= \dfrac{19\pi}{12}\]
Kyun: zarb mein angles jama hote hain (kitab ne yeh \(\cos(A + B)\) aur \(\sin(A + B)\) ke formulas se saabit kiya hai). Fractions jama karne ke liye common denominator 12 liya.

Principal argument
\[\dfrac{19\pi}{12} - 2\pi = -\dfrac{5\pi}{12}\]
\[z_1 z_2 = 45\left(\cos\dfrac{5\pi}{12} - i\sin\dfrac{5\pi}{12}\right)\]
Kyun: \(\frac{19\pi}{12}\) \(\pi\) se bara hai, yani principal range se bahar. Ek poora chakkar (\(2\pi\)) minus karne se direction wohi rehti hai aur angle range mein aa jata hai. Answer key ki form \(45\,\text{cis}\,\frac{19\pi}{12}\) bhi bilkul yahi number hai.
Dhyan dein: \(\cos(-\theta) = \cos\theta\) aur \(\sin(-\theta) = -\sin\theta\), is liye form mein '+' ki jagah '−' aa gaya.

Rectangular form
\(\frac{5\pi}{12} = 75^{\circ}\):
\[\cos 75^{\circ} = \dfrac{\sqrt{6} - \sqrt{2}}{4} \approx 0.2588\]
\[\sin 75^{\circ} = \dfrac{\sqrt{6} + \sqrt{2}}{4} \approx 0.9659\]
\[x = 45 \cdot \dfrac{\sqrt{6} - \sqrt{2}}{4} \approx 11.65\]
\[y = -45 \cdot \dfrac{\sqrt{6} + \sqrt{2}}{4} \approx -43.47\]
Kyun: \(\cos 75^{\circ}\) aur \(\sin 75^{\circ}\) ki exact values \(\cos(45^{\circ} + 30^{\circ})\) aur \(\sin(45^{\circ} + 30^{\circ})\) se aati hain; angle \(-75^{\circ}\) hai, is liye y negative.

Tasdeeq (check):
Ab wohi zarb rectangular form mein kar ke dekhte hain:
\((-6.364 - 6.364i)(2.5 + 4.330i)\)
\[= (-15.91 + 27.56) + (-27.56 - 15.91)i\]
\[\approx 11.65 - 43.47i\]
Dono tareeqon se ek hi jawab aaya. Sahi. (Rectangular zarb mein \(i^{2} = -1\) istemal hua.)

blocks.prompt: 4 (iv) If \(z_1 = 9\left(\cos\frac{5\pi}{4} + i\sin\frac{5\pi}{4}\right)\) and \(z_2 = 5\left(\cos\frac{\pi}{3} + i\sin\frac{\pi}{3}\right)\), find \(\frac{z_1}{z_2}\).

blocks.prompt: 8. Find the modulus and argument of \(z = -2 - 2i\).
blocks.explanation: Yeh seedha modulus aur argument ka sawal hai. Modulus yani point \((-2, -2)\) ka O se faasla, aur argument yani polar axis se us ki direction. Modulus \(\sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2}}\) se aasaani se nikalta hai; asal imtihan argument ka hai. Dhyan dein: yahan calculator ka \(\tan^{-1}(y/x)\) akela \(45^{\circ}\) deta hai, jo first quadrant hai, jab ke point third quadrant mein hai. Plan: modulus, phir reference angle, phir quadrant se principal argument.
steps:
Given (diya gaya hai): \(z = -2 - 2i\), yani \(x = -2\), \(y = -2\).
To find (maloom karna hai): \(|z|\) aur \(\arg z\).
Method (tareeqa): \(|z| = \sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2}}\); argument ke liye pehle reference angle, phir quadrant. Kitab principal argument \((-\pi, \pi]\) mein leti hai.

Qadam 1: Modulus
\[|z| = \sqrt{(-2)^{2} + (-2)^{2}}\]
\[= \sqrt{4 + 4} = \sqrt{8} = 2\sqrt{2}\]
Kyun: modulus point \((-2, -2)\) ka O se faasla hai (Pythagoras). Square karne se minus khatam ho jate hain, kyunke faasla negative nahi hota. \(\sqrt{8} = \sqrt{4 \times 2} = 2\sqrt{2}\).

Qadam 2: Quadrant aur reference angle
\[\alpha = \tan^{-1}\left|\dfrac{-2}{-2}\right| = \tan^{-1} 1 = \dfrac{\pi}{4}\]
Dono \(x\) aur \(y\) negative hain, is liye point teesre (third) quadrant mein hai.
Kyun: \(\tan^{-1}(y/x)\) sirf x-axis ke saath chhota (acute) angle deta hai; x aur y ke signs batate hain ke point kis quadrant mein hai. Socho: \(\frac{-2}{-2} = 1\) aur \(\frac{2}{2} = 1\) dono barabar hain, lekin points ulti jagahon par hain.

Qadam 3: Principal argument
\[\arg z = -\pi + \dfrac{\pi}{4} = -\dfrac{3\pi}{4}\]
Kyun: third quadrant mein principal argument (range \((-\pi, \pi]\)) clockwise ghoom kar milta hai: \(-(\pi - \alpha)\).
Anticlockwise jaayein to \(\pi + \frac{\pi}{4} = \frac{5\pi}{4}\) aata hai, jo wohi direction hai. Tamam arguments: \(-\frac{3\pi}{4} + 2n\pi\), jo answer key ke \(\frac{5\pi}{4} + 2n\pi\), \(n \in \mathbb{Z}\) wala hi set hai. Is liye answer key ka jawab bhi sahi hai, bas principal value nahi.
Dhyan dein: \(\frac{\pi}{4}\) likh dena (calculator wala) sab se aam ghalti hai; woh \(2 + 2i\) ka argument hai.

Tasdeeq (check):
\[2\sqrt{2}\left(\cos\left(-\tfrac{3\pi}{4}\right) + i\sin\left(-\tfrac{3\pi}{4}\right)\right)\]
\[= 2\sqrt{2}\left(-\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} - \tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}i\right)\]
\[= -2 - 2i \;✓\]
Wapas \(-2 - 2i\) mil gaya.
blocks.final_answer: \(|z| = 2\sqrt{2}\); principal \(\arg z = -\frac{3\pi}{4}\) (aam taur par \(\arg z = \frac{5\pi}{4} + 2n\pi\), wohi direction). Yani point O se \(2\sqrt{2}\) door, third quadrant ke beech (diagonal) par hai.

blocks.text: Sawal 9

blocks.prompt: 9. Write the equation \(\arg(\overline{z} - 2 + i) = \frac{2\pi}{3}\) in cartesian form, if \(z = x + iy\).
blocks.explanation: Yeh 'locus' ka sawal hai. Locus (points ka raasta) ka matlab hai: woh tamam points jo ek shart poori karte hain. Yahan shart argument ki shakal mein di gayi hai, aur humein use x aur y wali aam equation (cartesian form) mein badalna hai. Plan: \(\overline{z} - 2 + i\) ko (real part) + (imaginary part)i mein likhein, phir \(\tan\theta = \frac{\text{imaginary}}{\text{real}}\) lagayein, aur aakhir mein quadrant ki shart na bhoolein, kyunke tan ek hi value do ulti directions ko deta hai.
steps:
Given (diya gaya hai): \(z = x + iy\) aur \(\arg(\overline{z} - 2 + i) = \frac{2\pi}{3}\).
To find (maloom karna hai): x aur y mein equation (cartesian form).
Method (tareeqa): agar \(\arg(a + ib) = \theta\) ho to \(\tan\theta = b/a\), aur point \((a, b)\) usi quadrant mein hona chahiye jis mein \(\theta\) hai.

Qadam 1: Number ko a + ib form mein likhein
\[\overline{z} = x - iy\]
\[\overline{z} - 2 + i = (x - 2) + (1 - y)i\]
Kyun: conjugate (jora: imaginary part ka sign ulat dena) se \(\overline{z} = x - iy\). Phir real hisse \((x - 2)\) aur imaginary hisse \((-y + 1)\) alag alag ikatthe kiye.
Dhyan dein: yahan \(z\) nahi, \(\overline{z}\) hai. Agar \(z\) le liya to imaginary part \(y + 1\) ban jayega aur poora jawab badal jayega.

Qadam 2: Argument ka tan lagayein
\[\tan\dfrac{2\pi}{3} = \dfrac{1 - y}{x - 2}\]
\[\tan\dfrac{2\pi}{3} = -\sqrt{3}\]
\[\dfrac{1 - y}{x - 2} = -\sqrt{3}\]
Kyun: \(a + ib\) ka argument \(\theta\) ho to \(\tan\theta = b/a\). \(\frac{2\pi}{3} = 120^{\circ}\) second quadrant mein hai jahan tan negative hota hai: \(\tan 120^{\circ} = -\tan 60^{\circ} = -\sqrt{3}\).

Qadam 3: y ko akela karein
\[1 - y = -\sqrt{3}(x - 2)\]
\[1 - y = -\sqrt{3}x + 2\sqrt{3}\]
\[y = \sqrt{3}x - 2\sqrt{3} + 1\]
Kyun: pehle cross-multiply kiya (\(x - 2\) ko doosri taraf zarb), phir bracket khola, phir \(y\) ko ek taraf aur baqi sab doosri taraf. Yeh ek seedhi line ki equation hai jis ka slope \(\sqrt{3}\) hai.

Qadam 4: Quadrant ki shart
Angle \(\frac{2\pi}{3}\) second quadrant mein hai, is liye real part \(x - 2 < 0\) aur imaginary part \(1 - y > 0\), yani \(x < 2\).
Kyun: \(\tan\theta = -\sqrt{3}\) angle \(-\frac{\pi}{3}\) (fourth quadrant) ke liye bhi sach hai. Line ka woh aadha hissa argument \(-\frac{\pi}{3}\) ka hai, \(\frac{2\pi}{3}\) ka nahi. Is liye locus line ka sirf woh hissa hai jahan \(x < 2\): yeh ek ray hai jo \((2, 1)\) se shuru hoti hai (yeh point khud shaamil nahi, kyunke wahan number 0 ban jata hai jis ka argument hota hi nahi).
Dhyan dein: zyada tar students yahan ruk jaate hain aur poori line likh dete hain. Poori line likhna aam taur par qabool hai, lekin samajhna zaroori hai ke asal mein aadhi line hi sahi hai.

Tasdeeq (check): \(x = 1\) lein; line se \(y = 1 - \sqrt{3}\).
\[\overline{z} - 2 + i = (1 - 2) + (1 - 1 + \sqrt{3})i\]
\[= -1 + \sqrt{3}\,i\]
Yeh point second quadrant mein hai aur \(\tan\theta = -\sqrt{3}\), is liye \(\theta = \frac{2\pi}{3}\). Sahi.
blocks.final_answer: \(y = \sqrt{3}x - 2\sqrt{3} + 1\) (sirf woh hissa jahan \(x < 2\)): \((2, 1)\) se baayein taraf jaane wali ek seedhi ray.

blocks.text: Sawal 10

blocks.prompt: 10. If \(z = x + iy\) and \(\arg\left(\frac{\overline{z} - 1 + 2i}{\overline{z} + 1 - 2i}\right) = \frac{9\pi}{4}\), show that \(x^{2} + y^{2} - 4x + 2y - 5 = 0\).
blocks.explanation: Yeh 'show that' (saabit karein) wala locus ka sawal hai, jis mein ek fraction ka argument diya hai. Pehli baat: \(\frac{9\pi}{4}\) dekh kar ghabrayein nahi; yeh \(2\pi + \frac{\pi}{4}\) hai, yani ek poora chakkar aur \(\frac{\pi}{4}\). Is liye fraction ki direction \(\frac{\pi}{4}\) hai, jahan real part aur imaginary part barabar hote hain. Plan: upar aur neeche ko a + ib mein likhein, neeche ke conjugate se zarb kar ke neeche ko real banayein, phir real part = imaginary part rakh dein.
steps:
Given (diya gaya hai): \(z = x + iy\) aur \(\arg\left(\frac{\overline{z} - 1 + 2i}{\overline{z} + 1 - 2i}\right) = \frac{9\pi}{4}\).
To prove (saabit karna hai): \(x^{2} + y^{2} - 4x + 2y - 5 = 0\).
Method (tareeqa): agar \(\arg w = \frac{\pi}{4}\) ho aur \(w = a + ib\), to \(\tan\frac{\pi}{4} = \frac{b}{a} = 1\), yani \(a = b\) (aur dono positive).

Qadam 1: \(\frac{9\pi}{4}\) ka matlab kya hai?
\[\dfrac{9\pi}{4} = 2\pi + \dfrac{\pi}{4}\]
Kyun: \(2\pi\) ek poora chakkar hai jo hamein wapas usi direction par le aata hai, jaise ghari ki sui 12 ghante baad wahin aa jaati hai. Is liye fraction \(\frac{\pi}{4}\) ki direction (first quadrant) mein hai. Note: \(\frac{9\pi}{4}\) principal value nahi; is ki principal value \(\frac{\pi}{4}\) hai.

Qadam 2: Upar aur neeche ko a + ib form mein likhein
\[\overline{z} = x - iy\]
\[\text{Top} = (x - 1) + (2 - y)i\]
\[\text{Bottom} = (x + 1) - (y + 2)i\]
Kyun: \(\overline{z} = x - iy\) rakha, phir real aur imaginary hisse alag ikatthe kiye. Upar: \(x - iy - 1 + 2i\); neeche: \(x - iy + 1 - 2i\).
Dhyan dein: neeche ka imaginary part \(-y - 2 = -(y + 2)\) hai; minus ko bahar nikaalte waqt dono terms ka sign badalta hai.

Qadam 3: Neeche ke conjugate se zarb karein
Neeche ka conjugate: \((x + 1) + (y + 2)i\).
Naya neeche: \((x + 1)^{2} + (y + 2)^{2}\), jo ek positive real number hai.
Kyun: kisi number ko us ke conjugate se zarb karein to \(a^{2} + b^{2}\) milta hai, jis mein i nahi hota. Is ke baad fraction = (naya upar)/(positive number), aur positive number se taqseem direction nahi badalta. Is liye ab sirf naye upar ki direction dekhni hai.

Qadam 4: Naye upar ka real part
\((a + bi)(c + di)\) ka real part \(= ac - bd\) hota hai, jahan \(a = x - 1\), \(b = 2 - y\), \(c = x + 1\), \(d = y + 2\).
\[\text{Re} = (x - 1)(x + 1) - (2 - y)(2 + y)\]
\[= x^{2} - 1 - (4 - y^{2})\]
\[= x^{2} + y^{2} - 5\]
Kyun: \((x-1)(x+1)\) aur \((2-y)(2+y)\) dono 'difference of squares' (\((p - q)(p + q) = p^{2} - q^{2}\)) hain. Real part mein \(-bd\) is liye aata hai ke \(bi \cdot di = bd\,i^{2} = -bd\).

Qadam 5: Naye upar ka imaginary part
Imaginary part \(= ad + bc\):
\[\text{Im} = (x - 1)(y + 2) + (2 - y)(x + 1)\]
\[= xy + 2x - y - 2\]
\[\quad + 2x + 2 - xy - y\]
\[= 4x - 2y\]
Kyun: dono brackets khole; \(xy\) aur \(-xy\) cancel ho gaye, aur \(-2\), \(+2\) bhi cancel ho gaye.
Dhyan dein: bracket kholte waqt har term ko har term se zarb karein (chaar products); ek term chhoot jaana aam ghalti hai.

Qadam 6: Real part = imaginary part rakhein
\[x^{2} + y^{2} - 5 = 4x - 2y\]
\[x^{2} + y^{2} - 4x + 2y - 5 = 0\]
Kyun: direction \(\frac{\pi}{4}\) ka matlab \(\tan\frac{\pi}{4} = \frac{\text{Im}}{\text{Re}} = 1\), yani Re = Im. Phir sab terms ek taraf le aaye. (Bilkul sahi baat yeh hai ke points ke liye \(4x - 2y > 0\) bhi chahiye, is liye locus is circle ka ek hissa (arc) hai.)

Tasdeeq (check): \(x = 5, y = 0\) circle par hai (\(25 - 20 - 5 = 0\)). Is ke liye \(\overline{z} = 5\):
\[\dfrac{5 - 1 + 2i}{5 + 1 - 2i} = \dfrac{4 + 2i}{6 - 2i}\]
\[= \dfrac{(4 + 2i)(6 + 2i)}{40} = \dfrac{20 + 20i}{40}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}i\]
Real part = imaginary part > 0, is liye argument \(\frac{\pi}{4}\) hai (\(\frac{9\pi}{4}\) wali direction). Sahi.
blocks.final_answer: Saabit ho gaya: \(x^{2} + y^{2} - 4x + 2y - 5 = 0\). Yeh ek circle ki equation hai (centre \((2, -1)\), radius \(\sqrt{10}\)).

blocks.text: Sawal 11

blocks.prompt: 11. If \(z = x + iy\) and \(\arg(z - 2 - 3i) - \arg(z + 2 + 3i) = 2\pi\), show that \(2y = 3x\).
blocks.explanation: Yeh bhi locus ka 'show that' sawal hai, lekin is mein do arguments ka farq diya hai. Pehla rule: \(\arg z_1 - \arg z_2 = \arg\frac{z_1}{z_2}\), yani do arguments ka farq ek fraction ka argument ban jata hai. Doosri baat: \(2\pi\) ek poora chakkar hai, yani 0 wali direction: fraction ek positive real number hona chahiye. Plan: fraction ko a + ib mein likhein, us ka imaginary part 0 rakhein, aur aakhir mein imaandari se check karein ke 'positive' wali shart kya kehti hai.
steps:
Given (diya gaya hai): \(z = x + iy\), \(\arg(z - 2 - 3i) - \arg(z + 2 + 3i) = 2\pi\).
To prove (saabit karna hai): \(2y = 3x\).
Method (tareeqa): \(\arg z_1 - \arg z_2 = \arg\frac{z_1}{z_2}\) (polar form ke quotient rule se).

Qadam 1: Dono arguments ko jorein
\[\arg\left(\dfrac{z - 2 - 3i}{z + 2 + 3i}\right) = 2\pi\]
Kyun: polar form mein taqseem karne se arguments minus hote hain; isi ko ulta parhein to arguments ka farq quotient ka argument hai.

Qadam 2: \(2\pi\) argument ka matlab
\(2\pi\) ek poora chakkar hai, yani 0 wali direction: positive real axis. Is liye quotient ek positive real number hona chahiye: imaginary part \(= 0\) aur real part \(> 0\).
Kyun: argument poore chakkaron tak hi tay hota hai, is liye \(2\pi\) aur \(0\) ek hi direction hain. (Agar dono arguments principal values \((-\pi, \pi]\) mein hon to un ka farq \(-2\pi\) aur \(2\pi\) ke beech hi rehta hai aur kabhi bilkul \(2\pi\) nahi ho sakta; is liye sawal sirf is 'poore chakkar' wale matlab se hi samajh aata hai.)

Qadam 3: Upar aur neeche ko a + ib form mein likhein
\[z - 2 - 3i = (x - 2) + (y - 3)i\]
\[z + 2 + 3i = (x + 2) + (y + 3)i\]
Kyun: \(z = x + iy\) rakha aur real aur imaginary hisse alag ikatthe kiye.

Qadam 4: Upar ko neeche ke conjugate se zarb karein
Neeche ka conjugate: \((x + 2) - (y + 3)i\). \((a + bi)(c - di)\) ka imaginary part \(bc - ad\) hota hai:
\[\text{Im} = (y - 3)(x + 2) - (x - 2)(y + 3)\]
\[= (xy + 2y - 3x - 6)\]
\[\quad - (xy + 3x - 2y - 6)\]
\[= 4y - 6x\]
Kyun: naya neeche \((x+2)^{2} + (y+3)^{2}\) positive hai, is liye quotient tabhi real hoga jab yeh imaginary part 0 ho. Hamein poora zarb karne ki zaroorat nahi, sirf imaginary part chahiye.
Dhyan dein: doosre bracket se pehle minus hai, is liye us ke andar har term ka sign badalta hai: \(-xy - 3x + 2y + 6\).

Qadam 5: Imaginary part ko zero rakhein
\[4y - 6x = 0\]
\[4y = 6x\]
\[2y = 3x\]
Kyun: real number ka imaginary part nahi hota (0 hota hai); phir dono taraf 2 se taqseem kiya.
Geometry se samjhein: \(\arg(z - 2 - 3i)\) point \(2 + 3i\) se z ki taraf direction hai aur \(\arg(z + 2 + 3i)\) point \(-2 - 3i\) se z ki taraf. Dono directions bilkul ek jaisi tabhi hoti hain jab z, \(2 + 3i\) aur \(-2 - 3i\) ek hi seedhi line par hon, aur in do points se guzarne wali line \(y = \frac{3}{2}x\), yani \(2y = 3x\) hai.

Qadam 6: 'Positive' wali shart ka imaandar check
Naye upar ka real part:
\[(x - 2)(x + 2) + (y - 3)(y + 3)\]
\[= x^{2} + y^{2} - 13\]
Yeh positive hona chahiye, is liye \(x^{2} + y^{2} > 13\).
Kyun: points \(2 + 3i\) aur \(-2 - 3i\) line \(2y = 3x\) par hain, O se \(\sqrt{13}\) door. In ke darmiyan (maslan \(z = 0\)) quotient \(\frac{-2 - 3i}{2 + 3i} = -1\) hai, jo negative hai: wahan arguments ka farq \(\pi\) hai, \(2\pi\) nahi. In se bahar (maslan \(z = 4 + 6i\)) quotient \(\frac{2 + 3i}{6 + 9i} = \frac{1}{3} > 0\). Sahi.
Teacher ki baat: saabit karne wale sawal mein yeh shart likhna zaroori nahi, lekin yeh samajh lena ke line ka har point kaam nahi karta, achhe student ki nishani hai.
blocks.final_answer: Saabit ho gaya: \(2y = 3x\). (Shart poori karne wala har point is line par hai; bilkul theek kahein to sirf line ke un hisson par jo \(-2 - 3i\) aur \(2 + 3i\) ko jorne wale tukre se bahar hain.)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Kya kitab ka daawa sahi hai? Haan, is matlab mein: agar arguments ke farq \(2\pi\) ko "poora chakkar, yani 0 wali direction" samjhein, to shart poori karne wala har \(z\) line \(2y = 3x\) par hi hai, aur sawal yahi saabit karne ko kehta hai. Lekin ulti baat sach nahi: line ka har point kaam nahi karta. \(-2 - 3i\) aur \(2 + 3i\) ke beech wale points par farq \(\pm\pi\) aata hai, aur dono end points par ek argument define hi nahi hota. Aur agar kitab ke principal arguments \((-\pi, \pi]\) sakhti se lein, to farq theek \(2\pi\) ho hi nahi sakta, yani koi \(z\) is equation ko poora nahi karta.
Sawal 12

blocks.prompt: 12. Solve the equation \(|z - 2i| = |\overline{z} + 2|\) for \(z = x + iy\).
blocks.explanation: Yeh do moduli (sizes) ke barabar hone ki equation hai. Yaad rakhiye, \(|z - a|\) ka matlab hai z ka point a se faasla. Yahan 'solve' ka matlab koi ek number nikaalna nahi, balke x aur y ka aapas mein rishta (relation) dhoondhna hai, yani woh points jo shart poori karte hain. Plan: dono taraf ko a + ib mein likhein, \(|a + ib| = \sqrt{a^{2} + b^{2}}\) lagayein, dono taraf square karein taake square root khatam ho, phir simplify karein.
steps:
Given (diya gaya hai): \(|z - 2i| = |\overline{z} + 2|\), \(z = x + iy\).
To find (maloom karna hai): x aur y ki equation.
Method (tareeqa): barabar moduli ke squares bhi barabar hote hain, aur square karne se square root hat jata hai.

Qadam 1: Dono taraf a + ib form mein likhein
\[z - 2i = x + (y - 2)i\]
\[\overline{z} + 2 = (x + 2) - yi\]
Kyun: \(\overline{z} = x - iy\) (conjugate mein imaginary part ka sign ulat jata hai); phir real aur imaginary hisse alag kiye.

Qadam 2: Dono moduli ka square
\[x^{2} + (y - 2)^{2} = (x + 2)^{2} + y^{2}\]
Kyun: \(|a + ib|^{2} = a^{2} + b^{2}\). Doosri taraf \(-y\) ka square \(y^{2}\) hai, is liye minus khatam ho gaya.

Qadam 3: Brackets kholein
\[x^{2} + y^{2} - 4y + 4\]
\[= x^{2} + 4x + 4 + y^{2}\]
Kyun: \((p \pm q)^{2} = p^{2} \pm 2pq + q^{2}\). Beech wali term \(2pq\) bhoolna sab se aam ghalti hai: \((y - 2)^{2}\) \(y^{2} + 4\) nahi, balke \(y^{2} - 4y + 4\) hai.

Qadam 4: Cancel kar ke simplify karein
\[-4y = 4x\]
\[y = -x\]
Kyun: \(x^{2}\), \(y^{2}\) aur 4 dono taraf hain, is liye cancel ho gaye; phir dono taraf \(-4\) se taqseem kiya.

Tasdeeq (check): \(z = 1 - i\) lein (\(x = 1\), \(y = -1\), jo \(y = -x\) par hai).
\[|1 - i - 2i| = |1 - 3i| = \sqrt{10}\]
\[|1 + i + 2| = |3 + i| = \sqrt{10} \;✓\]
Dono barabar hain. Answer key ka \(y = 2\) fail hota hai: \(z = 2i\) se \(|0| = 0\) magar \(|-2i + 2| = 2\sqrt{2}\).
Geometry se samjhein: \(|z - 2i|\) point \(2i\) se faasla hai aur \(|\overline{z} + 2| = |z + 2|\) point \(-2\) se faasla. Do points se barabar faasle wale points un ko jorne wali line ka perpendicular bisector (beech se seedhi kaatne wali line) hote hain, aur woh yahi \(y = -x\) hai.
blocks.final_answer: \(y = -x\), yani \(x + y = 0\): origin se guzarne wali line jis ka slope \(-1\) hai.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Answer key Sawal 12 ka jawab \(y = 2\) likhti hai. Yeh ghalat hai: \(z = 2i\) equation ko poora nahi karta. Sahi jawab \(y = -x\) (\(x + y = 0\)) hai.
Sawal 13

blocks.prompt: 13. For \(z = x - iy\), solve the equation \(|5z + 4 + i| = |5\overline{z} - 3 + 2i|\).
blocks.explanation: Yeh bhi Sawal 12 jaisa moduli ki barabari wala sawal hai. Ghor se dekhiye: hamare parhne ke mutabiq kitab yahan \(z = x - iy\) likhti hai (aam \(x + iy\) nahi), is liye \(\overline{z} = x + iy\) hoga. Hum sawal ko jaisa chhapa hai waisa hi hal karte hain, aur aakhir mein \(x + iy\) wala jawab bhi dete hain. Plan: dono taraf a + ib, moduli ka square, brackets kholna aur simplify.
steps:
Given (diya gaya hai): \(z = x - iy\), is liye \(\overline{z} = x + iy\); \(|5z + 4 + i| = |5\overline{z} - 3 + 2i|\).
To find (maloom karna hai): x aur y ka rishta.
Method (tareeqa): dono moduli ka square, \(|a + ib|^{2} = a^{2} + b^{2}\) se.

Qadam 1: Dono taraf a + ib form mein likhein
\[5z + 4 + i = (5x + 4) + (1 - 5y)i\]
\[5\overline{z} - 3 + 2i = (5x - 3) + (5y + 2)i\]
Kyun: \(5z = 5x - 5yi\) aur \(5\overline{z} = 5x + 5yi\); phir real aur imaginary hisse alag kiye.
Dhyan dein: pehli taraf imaginary part \(1 - 5y\) hai, kyunke \(z\) mein \(-iy\) hai.

Qadam 2: Dono moduli ka square
\[(5x + 4)^{2} + (1 - 5y)^{2}\]
\[= (5x - 3)^{2} + (5y + 2)^{2}\]
Kyun: barabar moduli ke squares barabar hote hain, aur square karne se square root hat jata hai.

Qadam 4: Cancel kar ke ikattha karein
\[40x - 10y + 17 = -30x + 20y + 13\]
\[70x - 30y + 4 = 0\]
\[35x - 15y + 2 = 0\]
Kyun: \(25x^{2}\) aur \(25y^{2}\) dono taraf hain, cancel ho gaye. Baqi: \(16 + 1 = 17\) aur \(9 + 4 = 13\). Sab ek taraf le aaye aur 2 se taqseem kiya.

Tasdeeq (check): \(x = -\frac{1}{5}\) lein; line se \(y = -\frac{1}{3}\), is liye \(z = -\frac{1}{5} + \frac{1}{3}i\), \(\overline{z} = -\frac{1}{5} - \frac{1}{3}i\).
\[5z + 4 + i = 3 + \tfrac{8}{3}i\]
\[|\cdot|^{2} = 9 + \tfrac{64}{9} = \tfrac{145}{9}\]
\[5\overline{z} - 3 + 2i = -4 + \tfrac{1}{3}i\]
\[|\cdot|^{2} = 16 + \tfrac{1}{9} = \tfrac{145}{9} \;✓\]
Dono squares barabar aaye. Sahi.

Agar aam \(z = x + iy\) muraad ho
Wohi kaam karne se milta hai:
\[70x + 30y + 4 = 0\]
\[35x + 15y + 2 = 0\]
Kyun: sirf har y wali term ka sign badalta hai, kyunke y ki jagah \(-y\) aa jata hai. Imtihan mein agar aap ke paper par \(x + iy\) chhapa ho to yeh jawab likhein.
blocks.final_answer: \(35x - 15y + 2 = 0\) (ek seedhi line), chhape hue \(z = x - iy\) ke liye. \(z = x + iy\) ke saath: \(35x + 15y + 2 = 0\).

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Answer key Sawal 13 ka jawab \(x = 1\) likhti hai. Yeh sawal ke kisi bhi matlab par poora nahi utarta: \(z = 1\) se \(|9 + i| = \sqrt{82}\) magar \(|2 + 2i| = \sqrt{8}\). Sahi jawab: chhape hue \(z = x - iy\) ke liye \(35x - 15y + 2 = 0\), aur \(z = x + iy\) ke liye \(35x + 15y + 2 = 0\).
Sawal 14

blocks.prompt: 14. Determine the set of points \(z = x + iy\) that satisfy the equation \(|3\overline{z} - 2 + i| = |3z + i|\).
blocks.explanation: Phir moduli ki barabari wali equation hai; 'set of points' ka matlab hai z ka locus, yani woh tamam points jo shart poori karte hain. Ab tak aap ne Sawal 12 aur 13 mein yeh tareeqa dekh liya hai, to khud koshish karein aur phir milayein. Plan: dono taraf a + ib, square, brackets kholna, cancel.
steps:
Given (diya gaya hai): \(z = x + iy\), \(|3\overline{z} - 2 + i| = |3z + i|\).
To find (maloom karna hai): points \((x, y)\) ka set.
Method (tareeqa): dono taraf \(|a + ib|^{2} = a^{2} + b^{2}\).

Qadam 1: Dono taraf a + ib form mein likhein
\[3\overline{z} - 2 + i = (3x - 2) + (1 - 3y)i\]
\[3z + i = 3x + (3y + 1)i\]
Kyun: \(3\overline{z} = 3x - 3yi\) aur \(3z = 3x + 3yi\); phir hisse alag kiye. Doosri taraf real part sirf \(3x\) hai, kyunke koi alag real number nahi.

Qadam 2: Dono moduli ka square
\[(3x - 2)^{2} + (1 - 3y)^{2}\]
\[= (3x)^{2} + (3y + 1)^{2}\]
Kyun: barabar moduli ke squares barabar.

Qadam 3: Brackets kholein
\[9x^{2} - 12x + 4 + 9y^{2} - 6y + 1\]
\[= 9x^{2} + 9y^{2} + 6y + 1\]
Kyun: \((p \pm q)^{2} = p^{2} \pm 2pq + q^{2}\). Beech wali term \(2pq\) bhoolna sab se aam ghalti hai: \((3x - 2)^{2}\) mein \(-12x\) zaroor aata hai.

Qadam 4: Cancel kar ke simplify karein
\[-12x - 6y + 4 = 6y\]
\[12x + 12y = 4\]
\[x + y = \dfrac{1}{3}\]
Kyun: \(9x^{2}\), \(9y^{2}\) aur 1 dono taraf cancel; phir x aur y wali terms ek taraf le aaye aur 12 se taqseem kiya.

Tasdeeq (check): \(z = \frac{1}{3}\) lein (\(x = \frac{1}{3}\), \(y = 0\)).
\[|1 - 2 + i| = |-1 + i| = \sqrt{2}\]
\[|1 + i| = \sqrt{2} \;✓\]
Dono barabar. Answer key ka \(y = \frac{1}{3}\) fail hota hai: \(z = 1 + \frac{1}{3}i\) se \(|1| = 1\) magar \(|3 + 2i| = \sqrt{13}\).
blocks.final_answer: Points ka set seedhi line \(x + y = \frac{1}{3}\) hai (yani \(3x + 3y = 1\), ya \(y = \frac{1}{3} - x\)).

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Answer key Sawal 14 ka jawab \(y = \frac{1}{3}\) likhti hai. Yeh ghalat hai: maslan \(z = 1 + \frac{1}{3}i\) equation ko poora nahi karta. Sahi set line \(x + y = \frac{1}{3}\) (\(y = \frac{1}{3} - x\)) hai.
Sawal 15

blocks.prompt: 15. An AC source supplies a voltage of \(V = 120\left(\cos\frac{\pi}{4} + i\sin\frac{\pi}{4}\right)\) volts to a circuit with impedance \(Z = \frac{1 + i\sqrt{3}}{2}\) ohms. Calculate the current in polar form.
blocks.explanation: Yeh real life application hai: AC circuits ka Ohm's law, \(V = IZ\) (jaise kitab ki Example 17 mein). V voltage hai, I current aur Z impedance (AC circuit mein current ki rukawat, jo complex number hoti hai). V aur Z diye hain, humein current \(I = V/Z\) polar form mein chahiye. Plan: Z ko bhi polar form mein badlein, kyunke taqseem polar form mein sab se aasaan hai: moduli taqseem, arguments minus.
steps:
Given (diya gaya hai): \(V = 120\left(\cos\frac{\pi}{4} + i\sin\frac{\pi}{4}\right)\) volts, \(Z = \frac{1 + i\sqrt{3}}{2}\) ohms.
To find (maloom karna hai): current \(I\) polar form mein.
Method (tareeqa): \(V = IZ\), is liye \(I = \frac{V}{Z}\); V pehle hi polar form mein hai, Z ko bhi kar lein.

Qadam 1: Z ka modulus
\[Z = \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}i\]
\[|Z| = \sqrt{\tfrac{1}{4} + \tfrac{3}{4}} = 1\]
Kyun: pehle Z ko alag parts mein likha, phir \(|a + ib| = \sqrt{a^{2} + b^{2}}\).

Qadam 2: Z ka argument
\[\tan\theta = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}/2}{1/2} = \sqrt{3}\]
\[\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{3}\]
\[Z = \cos\dfrac{\pi}{3} + i\sin\dfrac{\pi}{3}\]
Kyun: dono parts positive hain, is liye Z first quadrant mein hai aur \(\tan^{-1}\sqrt{3} = \frac{\pi}{3}\) hi sahi angle hai. Yeh wohi number hai jo Sawal 2(iii) mein tha.

Qadam 3: Taqseem karein
\[I = \dfrac{120}{1}\,(\cos\phi + i\sin\phi)\]
\[\phi = \tfrac{\pi}{4} - \tfrac{\pi}{3} = \tfrac{3\pi - 4\pi}{12}\]
\[\phi = -\tfrac{\pi}{12}\]
\[I = 120\left[\cos\left(-\tfrac{\pi}{12}\right) + i\sin\left(-\tfrac{\pi}{12}\right)\right]\]
Kyun: quotient rule: moduli taqseem (\(120 \div 1\)), arguments minus (V ka angle minus Z ka angle). Common denominator 12 liya: \(\frac{\pi}{4} = \frac{3\pi}{12}\), \(\frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{4\pi}{12}\).

Qadam 4: Signs saaf karein
\[I = 120\left(\cos\tfrac{\pi}{12} - i\sin\tfrac{\pi}{12}\right)\]
\[I \approx 115.91 - 31.06i\]
Kyun: \(\cos(-\theta) = \cos\theta\) aur \(\sin(-\theta) = -\sin\theta\). Yeh answer key ki form se milta hai. Negative argument ka matlab hai ke current voltage se thora 'peeche' (lag) hai.

Tasdeeq (check): \(IZ\) se V wapas aana chahiye.
\[IZ = 120 \cdot 1\,[\cos(-\tfrac{\pi}{12} + \tfrac{\pi}{3}) + i\sin(\cdots)]\]
\[-\tfrac{\pi}{12} + \tfrac{4\pi}{12} = \tfrac{3\pi}{12} = \tfrac{\pi}{4}\]
Is liye \(IZ = 120\left(\cos\frac{\pi}{4} + i\sin\frac{\pi}{4}\right) = V\). Sahi.
blocks.final_answer: \(I = 120\left(\cos\frac{\pi}{12} - i\sin\frac{\pi}{12}\right)\) amperes, yani modulus 120 A aur argument \(-\frac{\pi}{12}\) (\(\approx 115.91 - 31.06i\)).

blocks.text: Sawal 16

blocks.prompt: 16. An AC circuit has an impedance of \(Z = 3 - 6i\) ohms and is connected to a voltage source of \(V = 90 + 30i\) volts. Find the current in both rectangular and polar form.
blocks.explanation: Phir AC circuit ka Ohm's law: \(V = IZ\), is liye \(I = V/Z\). Is baar V aur Z dono rectangular form mein hain, is liye taqseem conjugate ke zariye karenge: upar aur neeche dono ko Z ke conjugate se zarb. Phir jawab ko polar form mein bhi likhna hai. Aakhir mein \(IZ = V\) se check karenge, jo answer key ki ghalti bhi pakar leta hai.
steps:
Given (diya gaya hai): \(Z = 3 - 6i\) ohms, \(V = 90 + 30i\) volts.
To find (maloom karna hai): current \(I\), rectangular aur polar dono forms mein.
Method (tareeqa): \(I = \frac{V}{Z}\); rectangular form mein taqseem ke liye upar neeche \(\overline{Z} = 3 + 6i\) se zarb.

Qadam 1: Taqseem ki tayyari
\[I = \dfrac{90 + 30i}{3 - 6i} \times \dfrac{3 + 6i}{3 + 6i}\]
Kyun: \((3 - 6i)(3 + 6i)\) ek real number hai, is liye neeche se i khatam ho jayega. \(\frac{3 + 6i}{3 + 6i} = 1\) hai, is liye value nahi badalti.

Qadam 2: Upar zarb karein
\[(90 + 30i)(3 + 6i)\]
\[= 270 + 540i + 90i + 180i^{2}\]
\[= 270 - 180 + 630i\]
\[= 90 + 630i\]
Kyun: chaar products (har term har term se), phir \(i^{2} = -1\), is liye \(180i^{2} = -180\).
Dhyan dein: \(+180i^{2}\) ko \(+180\) likh dena aam ghalti hai; \(i^{2}\) hamesha \(-1\) hai.

Qadam 3: Neeche zarb karein
\[(3 - 6i)(3 + 6i) = 9 + 36 = 45\]
Kyun: \((a - ib)(a + ib) = a^{2} + b^{2}\): \(9 + 36 = 45\). Middle terms cancel ho jaati hain.

Qadam 4: Taqseem karein
\[I = \dfrac{90 + 630i}{45} = 2 + 14i\]
Kyun: \(90 \div 45 = 2\) aur \(630 \div 45 = 14\); dono parts ko alag alag taqseem kiya.

Qadam 5: Polar form: modulus
\[|I| = \sqrt{2^{2} + 14^{2}} = \sqrt{200}\]
\[= 10\sqrt{2} \approx 14.14\]
Kyun: \(\sqrt{200} = \sqrt{100 \times 2} = 10\sqrt{2}\).

Qadam 6: Polar form: argument
\[\theta = \tan^{-1}\dfrac{14}{2} = \tan^{-1} 7\]
\[\theta \approx 81.87^{\circ}\]
\[I = 10\sqrt{2}(\cos 81.87^{\circ} + i\sin 81.87^{\circ})\]
Kyun: dono parts positive hain, I first quadrant mein hai, is liye calculator ka angle hi sahi hai (\(\approx 1.429\) rad).

Tasdeeq (check): \(IZ\) se V aana chahiye.
\[(2 + 14i)(3 - 6i)\]
\[= 6 - 12i + 42i - 84i^{2}\]
\[= 6 + 84 + 30i = 90 + 30i \;✓\]
Answer key ka \(18i\) fail hota hai: \(18i(3 - 6i) = 108 + 54i \neq V\).
blocks.final_answer: Rectangular form: \(I = 2 + 14i\) A; polar form: \(I = 10\sqrt{2}(\cos 81.87^{\circ} + i\sin 81.87^{\circ}) \approx 14.14\) A, \(81.87^{\circ}\) par.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Answer key Sawal 16 ka jawab "Rectangular form: \(0 + 18i\), Polar form: \(18\left(\cos\frac{\pi}{2} + i\sin\frac{\pi}{2}\right)\)" likhti hai. Yeh ghalat hai: \(18i \times (3 - 6i) = 108 + 54i\), \(90 + 30i\) nahi. Sahi current \(I = 2 + 14i = 10\sqrt{2}(\cos 81.87^{\circ} + i\sin 81.87^{\circ})\) hai.
Sawal 17

blocks.prompt: 17. Encrypt the word "CODE" by multiplying the complex encryption key \(k = 2 - i\). Then decrypt it back to the original word.
blocks.explanation: Yeh cryptography (khufia paigham ka ilm) ka sawal hai, jaise kitab ki Example 18 mein. Har letter ko ek number diya jata hai (A = 1, B = 2, ..., Z = 26) aur use complex number banaya jata hai jis ka imaginary part 0 ho. Encrypt (chhupana): har number ko key \(k\) se zarb karein. Decrypt (wapas parhna): k se taqseem karein, yani \(k^{-1}\) (multiplicative inverse, woh number jis se k ko zarb karein to 1 aaye) se zarb karein. Socho jaise taala aur chaabi: k se taala lagta hai aur \(k^{-1}\) se khulta hai.
steps:
Given (diya gaya hai): lafz CODE, key \(k = 2 - i\), aur A = 1, B = 2, ..., Z = 26 (Example 18 ki tarah).
To find (maloom karna hai): encrypted numbers, aur phir wapas asal lafz.
Method (tareeqa): encrypted \(= z \times k\); decrypted \(= (z \times k) \div k = (z \times k) \times k^{-1}\).

Qadam 1: Letters ko complex numbers banayein
\[C = 3 + 0i, \quad O = 15 + 0i\]
\[D = 4 + 0i, \quad E = 5 + 0i\]
Kyun: C teesra letter hai, O pandrahwan, D chautha, E paanchwan. Kitab har letter ko imaginary part 0 deti hai.

Qadam 2: Encrypt (k se zarb)
\[(3 + 0i)(2 - i) = 6 - 3i\]
\[(15 + 0i)(2 - i) = 30 - 15i\]
\[(4 + 0i)(2 - i) = 8 - 4i\]
\[(5 + 0i)(2 - i) = 10 - 5i\]
Kyun: real number ko \(2 - i\) se zarb karne se dono parts us number se zarb ho jaate hain (\(3 \times 2 = 6\), \(3 \times (-i) = -3i\)). Khufia paigham: \(6 - 3i,\ 30 - 15i,\ 8 - 4i,\ 10 - 5i\). Ab koi bhi yeh numbers dekh kar asaani se CODE nahi parh sakta.

Qadam 3: Key ka inverse nikaalein
\[k^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{2 - i} \times \dfrac{2 + i}{2 + i}\]
\[= \dfrac{2 + i}{4 + 1} = \dfrac{2 + i}{5}\]
Kyun: k se taqseem karna \(k^{-1}\) se zarb karne ke barabar hai. \(\frac{1}{2 - i}\) ke neeche i hai, is liye upar neeche conjugate \(2 + i\) se zarb kiya taake neeche real ho jaye: \((2 - i)(2 + i) = 4 - i^{2} = 4 + 1 = 5\).

Qadam 4: Pehla number poora decrypt karein
\[(6 - 3i) \cdot \dfrac{2 + i}{5}\]
\[= \dfrac{12 + 6i - 6i - 3i^{2}}{5}\]
\[= \dfrac{12 + 3}{5} = 3 \;\Rightarrow\; C\]
Kyun: \(i^{2} = -1\), is liye \(-3i^{2} = +3\); \(6i\) aur \(-6i\) cancel ho gaye aur wapas ek real number aaya, jo letter ki value hai: 3, yani C.
Dhyan dein: agar decrypt ke baad imaginary part 0 na aaye to samajh lein ke kahin hisaab mein ghalti hai.

Qadam 5: Baqi numbers decrypt karein
\[(30 - 15i)\cdot\dfrac{2 + i}{5} = \dfrac{75}{5} = 15 \Rightarrow O\]
\[(8 - 4i)\cdot\dfrac{2 + i}{5} = \dfrac{20}{5} = 4 \Rightarrow D\]
\[(10 - 5i)\cdot\dfrac{2 + i}{5} = \dfrac{25}{5} = 5 \Rightarrow E\]
Kyun: bilkul Qadam 4 wala kaam (maslan \(30 \cdot 2 + 15 = 75\)). Poori table jawab ke neeche di gayi hai.

Tasdeeq (check): \(k \cdot k^{-1} = (2 - i)\cdot\frac{2 + i}{5} = \frac{4 + 1}{5} = 1\), is liye \(k^{-1}\) se zarb karna k se zarb ko bilkul ulta kar deta hai.
Kyun: \(z \times k \times k^{-1} = z \times 1 = z\). Yahi wajah hai ke asal lafz bina kisi kami ke wapas mil jata hai.

blocks.text: Sawal 18

blocks.prompt: 18. Consider the complex encryption key \(k = 3 - 3i\). Encrypt the word "QUIZ", and then recover the original word using the inverse of the key.
blocks.explanation: Yeh bilkul Sawal 17 wala tareeqa hai, bas key ab \(k = 3 - 3i\) hai. Encrypt: har letter ki value ko k se zarb. Asal lafz wapas: inverse \(k^{-1}\) se zarb, jaisa sawal khud kehta hai. Is key mein ek khoobsurti hai: \(3 - 3i = 3(1 - i)\), jis se hisaab bohat chhota ho jata hai.
steps:
Given (diya gaya hai): lafz QUIZ, key \(k = 3 - 3i\), A = 1, ..., Z = 26.
To find (maloom karna hai): encrypted numbers, phir \(k^{-1}\) se asal lafz.
Method (tareeqa): encrypted \(= z \times k\); wapas \(= (z \times k) \times k^{-1}\).

Qadam 1: Letters ko complex numbers banayein
\[Q = 17 + 0i, \quad U = 21 + 0i\]
\[I = 9 + 0i, \quad Z = 26 + 0i\]
Kyun: Q satrahwan letter hai, U ikkeeswan, I nawan, Z chhabbeeswan (aakhri). Ginti mein ghalti na ho, is liye alphabet ungliyon par gin kar check kar lein.

Qadam 2: Encrypt (k se zarb)
\[17(3 - 3i) = 51 - 51i\]
\[21(3 - 3i) = 63 - 63i\]
\[9(3 - 3i) = 27 - 27i\]
\[26(3 - 3i) = 78 - 78i\]
Kyun: letter ki value ko k ke dono parts se zarb kiya.

Qadam 3: Key ka inverse
\[k^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{3 - 3i} \times \dfrac{3 + 3i}{3 + 3i}\]
\[= \dfrac{3 + 3i}{9 + 9} = \dfrac{3 + 3i}{18}\]
\[= \dfrac{1 + i}{6}\]
Kyun: conjugate \(3 + 3i\) se upar neeche zarb kiya taake neeche real ho jaye: \(9 + 9 = 18\). Phir upar neeche se common factor 3 cancel kiya.

Qadam 4: Pehla letter wapas laayein
\[(51 - 51i)\cdot\dfrac{1 + i}{6} = \dfrac{51(1 - i)(1 + i)}{6}\]
\[= \dfrac{51 \times 2}{6} = 17 \;\Rightarrow\; Q\]
Kyun: \(51 - 51i = 51(1 - i)\), aur \((1 - i)(1 + i) = 1 - i^{2} = 1 + 1 = 2\). Phir \(\frac{102}{6} = 17\), yani Q.

Qadam 5: Baqi letters
\[(63 - 63i)\cdot\dfrac{1 + i}{6} = \dfrac{126}{6} = 21 \Rightarrow U\]
\[(27 - 27i)\cdot\dfrac{1 + i}{6} = \dfrac{54}{6} = 9 \Rightarrow I\]
\[(78 - 78i)\cdot\dfrac{1 + i}{6} = \dfrac{156}{6} = 26 \Rightarrow Z\]
Kyun: har encrypted number (value)\((1 - i)\cdot 3\) hai, is liye har baar wohi factor \(\frac{2}{6}\) aata hai aur nateeja \(\text{value} \times 3 \times \frac{2}{6} = \text{value}\).

Tasdeeq (check): \(k \cdot k^{-1} = (3 - 3i)\cdot\frac{1 + i}{6} = \frac{3(1 - i)(1 + i)}{6} = \frac{6}{6} = 1\).
Kyun: inverse ki pehchaan yahi hai ke key se zarb karne par 1 aaye; isi liye wapas asal values milti hain.

blocks.text: Sawal 19

blocks.prompt: 19. Encrypt the word "CLASS" by adding the complex encryption key \(k = -3 + 4i\). Then decrypt it back to the original word.
blocks.explanation: Is baar key zarb nahi balke jama (add) ki jaati hai. Encrypt: \(z + k\). Decrypt: k ko minus karna, yani us ka additive inverse \(-k\) (woh number jo k ke saath jama ho kar 0 de) jama karna. Yeh Sawal 17-18 se aasaan hai, kyunke jama mein sirf real se real aur imaginary se imaginary jorna hota hai.
steps:
Given (diya gaya hai): lafz CLASS, key \(k = -3 + 4i\), A = 1, ..., Z = 26.
To find (maloom karna hai): encrypted numbers, phir wapas lafz.
Method (tareeqa): encrypted \(= z + k\); decrypted \(= (z + k) - k = (z + k) + (3 - 4i)\).

Qadam 1: Letters ko complex numbers banayein
\[C = 3 + 0i, \quad L = 12 + 0i\]
\[A = 1 + 0i, \quad S = 19 + 0i\]
Kyun: C teesra, L barhwan, A pehla, S unneeswan letter hai (S do baar aata hai).

Qadam 2: Encrypt (k jama karein)
\[3 + (-3 + 4i) = 0 + 4i\]
\[12 + (-3 + 4i) = 9 + 4i\]
\[1 + (-3 + 4i) = -2 + 4i\]
\[19 + (-3 + 4i) = 16 + 4i\]
Kyun: real parts aur imaginary parts alag alag jama kiye: real part mein \(-3\) aur imaginary mein \(4i\). Paigham: \(4i,\ 9 + 4i,\ -2 + 4i,\ 16 + 4i,\ 16 + 4i\).
Dhyan dein: \(3 + (-3) = 0\), is liye C ka code sirf \(4i\) hai; real part 0 likhna na bhoolein.

Qadam 3: Decryption key
\[-k = -(-3 + 4i) = 3 - 4i\]
Kyun: \(k + (-k) = 0\), is liye \(-k\) jama karna k jama karne ko ulta kar deta hai. Minus bracket ke dono hisson par lagta hai: \(-(-3) = 3\) aur \(-(4i) = -4i\).

Qadam 4: Decrypt (\(3 - 4i\) jama karein)
\[(0 + 4i) + (3 - 4i) = 3 \Rightarrow C\]
\[(9 + 4i) + (3 - 4i) = 12 \Rightarrow L\]
\[(-2 + 4i) + (3 - 4i) = 1 \Rightarrow A\]
\[(16 + 4i) + (3 - 4i) = 19 \Rightarrow S\]
Kyun: \(4i\) aur \(-4i\) cancel ho jaate hain, aur har letter ki asal value bachti hai. Aakhri S chauthe wale jaisa hi hai.

Tasdeeq (check): \(k + (-k) = (-3 + 4i) + (3 - 4i) = 0\).
Teacher ki baat: dekhiye, ek jaise letters (S, S) ka code bhi ek jaisa aaya, aur har code ka imaginary part \(4i\) hi hai. Is liye jama wali key zarb wali key se kam mehfooz hai: koi bhi pattern pakar sakta hai.
